Marissa — copying thoughts from pricing/finance:

- For a 24-month, 120-GPU blended commit (assume 65% baseline sustained): recommended discount band = 28–32% off list (depends on SKU mix and guaranteed utilization profile).
- If the discount requested exceeds 30% we need an executive approval (Head of Sales + CFO sign-off).

GPU-price collar guidance (suggested construct):
- Band 0 (price change within +/-15%): no adjustment to customer billing (we treat as normal market noise).
- Band 1 (price up 15–30%): apply credit-based smoothing over the next quarter (one-time credit or increased capacity at existing price until reconciled).
- Band 2 (price up >30%): allow pass-through adjustment to per-unit price (with 30-day notice) OR offer an alternative: shorter credit+reprice if Helio prefers predictability.
- Downside (price decreases >15%): automatic rebate to Helio at renewal or an immediate pro-rated credit for unlocked capacity.

Operational guardrails: staged activation is OK — recommend tranches: 50% on signing, 25% at 6 months (conditional on utilization hitting 60% for prior 30 days), 25% at 12 months. That preserves runway and reduces immediate capital exposure.

I attached the pricing model used for these scenarios (pricing_model_helio.xlsx) — populate approximate GPU-hour rates and I will run sensitivity curves. Also link to HubSpot record: HS-11245.

-David

Agree with David. A couple of practical notes from deal ops / legal perspective:
- Recommend we include both a price-collar (credit smoothing) AND an escape valve tied to a limited pass-through to keep the legal language simple. Legal prefers a 2-step (credit then pass-through) instead of immediate pass-through.
- If Helio wants >32% off list we should trade that for a longer commit (24+ months) and/or stricter staged activation (e.g., delayed final tranche until utilization demonstration).
- Approval path: standard — AE can approve up to 20% off list, Head of Sales (you) up to 30%, >30% requires CFO sign-off (David) + Head of Sales. If we add irrevocable credit escrow we may be able to increase discount by another 2–3% (requires finance sign-off).
- Ask Marissa to capture: baseline utilization assumption, SKU mix, target start date, and explicit tranche triggers; we'll convert to term-sheet language.

Karthik

Nate — thanks for the clarity and for sharing the traffic profile earlier. Per internal alignment, here's a short mutual action plan and a proposed term structure for Helio: 

1) Proposal (subject to final SKU mapping): 18-month staged commitment starting Q1 2028 for a blended 110–130 GPU tranche (initial activation = 50% on signing, 25% at 6 months conditional on utilization, final 25% at 12 months). Estimated discount: 26–30% off list depending on final SKU mix.

2) Price-collar mechanics: 
- Market move within +/-15%: no change.
- Market up 15–30%: 60-day credit smoothing (one-time credit applied across next billing cycle or option to receive incremental capacity at prior price while we reconcile).
- Market up >30%: pass-through option with 30-day notice (or Helio can elect a credit instead). Downside savings >15% credited at renewal or pro-rated immediately.

3) Approval path and timing: AE (Marissa) can finalize up to 20% discount; Head of Sales (Karthik) + CFO (David) required if final discount >30%. Legal (Kimberly) will review collar language — Karthik, David: please confirm approvals chain and whether finance wants an escrow structure.

4) Next steps: Redwood to share a term-sheet draft and updated SOW reflecting tranches and collar by EOD Thursday. We will include the pricing model assumptions (attached). Helio to confirm SKU mix and provide signed confidentiality addendum if needed.

Attached: term-sheet-helio-draft.docx, draft_sow_v1.pdf

Would you like to sync for 30 minutes on Thursday to finalize details?

Best,
Marissa
